newsitem.title: DENMARK: Poll shows Danish support for EMU waning.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Danish support for EMU waning.

text.p: A new poll shows Danish support for Economic and Monetary Union falling again, after a rise logged in a December survey.

The Gallup poll, published in the Berlingske Tidende daily on Sunday, shows 41 percent of respondents believing that Denmark should reverse its 1993 decision not to join EMU, compared to 46 percent in December.
The survey, carried out between March 12-14, showed 49 percent in favour of maintaining the Danish 'no' to a common European currency, compared to 44 percent in December.
A survey by pollster Greens published on March 10 showed 55.6 percent of respondents opposed to EMU, with only 33.4 percent in favour and 10.9 percent undecided.
In a binding 1993 referendum Danish voters approved the Maastricht treaty on condition that their country reject EMU, common citizenship and joint defence.
The new Gallup poll shows a rise in support for a pan-European defence policy, to 50 percent from 46 percent in a June 1994 survey -- the last time the question was asked.

Opposition to European citizenship remains massive, at 73 percent, although down slightly from 1994's 77 percent. Latest polls on the question, "Should rejection (of EMU) be maintained or revoked so that Denmark can particpate in the common currency?"
